title: How to Write a Linear Equation From a Table

scenes.title: How do you turn a table into an equation?
body: The goal is not to guess the next number.
You are looking for the rule connecting x and y.
scenes.narration: Suppose a table gives you the points zero two, one five, and two eight. A lot of students look for the next number, but that is not the real idea. We want the rule connecting x to y. If the relationship is linear, that rule has two parts: how fast y changes, and where the pattern starts.

scenes.title: First find the rate of change
body: Here: Δx = 1 and Δy = 3 every time.
scenes.narration: Here is where students often mix things up: slope is not just the difference between y values. It is change in y divided by change in x. From the first row to the second, x goes up by one while y goes up by three, so the slope is three over one, which is three. The same change happens again, confirming the table is linear.

scenes.title: Now find the starting value
body: In y = mx + b, b is y when x = 0.
scenes.narration: Next we need the starting value. In y equals m x plus b, b means the value of y when x is zero. Students sometimes choose the first y-value automatically, but that only works if the first row actually has x equals zero. Here it does, and y equals two, so b equals two.

scenes.title: Build the equation from meaning
body: m = 3 tells how much y changes per 1 x.
b = 2 tells the value when x starts at 0.
scenes.narration: Now the formula is no longer something to memorize blindly. The three is the rate of change, and the two is the starting value. Put those meanings into y equals m x plus b, and we get y equals three x plus two.

scenes.title: Check the rule before you trust it
body: Use a row from the table.
scenes.narration: Always check the rule with one of the original rows. If x equals two, three times two plus two equals eight, exactly matching the table. So the equation is y equals three x plus two. The key idea is rate plus starting value, not just pattern spotting. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
